[EFFECT]
The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic effect on predicted bike demand. Contributions are most negative in the pre-dawn period, reaching their lowest point around 4–5 AM (SHAP values near –3.5), meaning those hours dramatically suppress rentals. Values rise sharply from around 6 AM, turn positive by roughly 8 AM, and peak near 5 PM (hour 17), where the contribution reaches approximately +1.0 in log space — the strongest boost to demand across the day. After that peak, contributions gradually decline through the evening and turn negative again by around 10–11 PM.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of the day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9. Its SHAP values span a range of nearly 4 log-units, making it far more influential on predicted demand than any other feature.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Fleet availability and staffing should be concentrated heavily around the late-afternoon peak (roughly 5 PM) and the morning ramp-up (7–9 AM), while overnight hours (midnight to 5 AM) can safely operate with minimal resources, as demand is predicted to be very low during those times.
